meta.name: GridWise adversarial note-generation suite
meta.conventions: Whole hours, start-inclusive/end-exclusive. Each note is scored against the live interpretation path (the configured LLM provider via /optimize-energy, followed by production guardrails). expected == null means the note must resolve to no_op.

notes.note: Rooftop solar output will drop to roughly one quarter of normal between 12 PM and 2 PM because of inverter firmware work.
Expect a 70% reduction in PV yield from 6 AM until 8 AM while the array is resurfaced.
The panels are being washed from noon until 2 PM, so usable solar should be treated as approximately one fifth of forecast during that time.
Solar generation is only about thirty percent of the usual forecast from 1 o'clock in the afternoon until 3 o'clock in the afternoon.
Between 7 PM and 9 PM tonight a shadow from the new crane cuts photovoltaic output to about half of the forecast.
Dust following the storm leaves PV arrays producing around 35% of forecast output between 9 AM and 11 AM.
From 2 in the afternoon to 4 in the afternoon an inverter fault reduces solar production to approximately one third of forecast.
Solar energy will be reduced by fifty percent from 5 PM to 7 PM because of panel cleaning.
Hold one hundred kWh in the battery from 5 PM until 8 PM for backup power.
Ensure at least a quarter of the battery's capacity stays stored from 9 PM until midnight for incident response.
The operations center requires a minimum battery level of 75 kWh between hours 18 and 21 tonight.
Keep 60% of battery capacity available at all times from 6 PM to 10 PM.
For grid-failure drills the battery must hold at least 20% of battery capacity from 3 PM until 6 PM.
Maintain a reserve of 120 kWh in storage from 10 PM until 2 AM for the laboratory freezers.
